from_statement_quote: DRAFT AUTHOR PROOF; independent review pending; no novelty claim. Let G be the simple undirected Cayley graph of <a,b | a^2=b^3=1> with the symmetric generating set {a,b,b^-1}. Each unordered a-edge appears once. In iid Bernoulli bond percolation, p_c=q, the unique root in (0,1) of 2q^2+2q^3-2q^4=1, with 0.63<q<0.64, and p_u=1. No infinite cluster exists at p<=q; for each fixed q<p<1 there are almost surely infinitely many; at p=1 there is one. The edge Cheeger constant is 1/3. For rho=||A||/3, the triangle Rayleigh bound gives 3*rho*p_c>=2q>1.26. This refutes universal satisfaction of the sufficient spectral criterion while proving this special case of nonuniqueness.
to_statement_quote: FALSE AUXILIARY CLAIM, recorded for refutation: every infinite connected nonamenable d-regular simple Cayley graph with independent Bernoulli bond percolation satisfies d*rho*p_c<1, where rho=||A||/d. This is stronger than the nonuniqueness conjecture and fails on the explicitly specified simple C_2*C_3 graph.
rationale: The triangle graph is nonamenable but 3*rho*p_c>1.26, so the stated universal inequality fails.

For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite connected d-regular simple Cayley graph G, write rho=||A_G||/d for simple random walk. If d*rho*p_c(G)<1, then p_c(G)<p_u(G). from_statement_quote: AUDIT CORRECTION (w559, 2026-10-10; independent review pending) of the 2026-09-07 C0047-A001 spectral route. For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite connected d-regular simple Cayley graph G, let rho=||A_G||/d denote the normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius. Benjamini-Schramm 1996, Theorem 4, printed p.76 (bond extension in section 2), and Juschenko-Nagnibeda 2015, Theorem 2, give the sufficient condition d*rho*p_c(G)<1 for p_c(G)<p_u(G). The original p_c<1/rho quotation omitted d and is not that criterion: it is automatic when rho<1 and p_c<=1. Nonamenability does not imply the repaired criterion for a prescribed generating set. In the simple Cayley graph C_2*C_3 with generators {a,b,b^-1}, p_c=q is the root of 2q^2+2q^3-2q^4=1 in (0.63,0.64), p_u=1, and ||A||>=2, so d*rho*p_c>1.26. This counterexample refutes only the stronger universal spectral bridge. An existence theorem for a favorable generating multiset does not establish the result for every prescribed simple generating set. The parent conjecture is not solved by this packet; current 2026 openness is UNKNOWN because a recent public full-result claim has not received a mathematical or comparator proof check here.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Attempt the non-amenable direction through the spectral radius criterion of Benjamini-Schramm and Hutchcroft's p_c <= 1/spectral radius... type bounds. Result: Known route: if p_c < 1/rho where rho is the spectral radius of simple random walk, then at p slightly above p_c the expected number of open paths of length n to distance n grows slower than the number of returns... this gives p_c < p_u for graphs where p_c(G) < 1/(rho ... ) and is the content of the Benjamini-Schramm 1996 criterion p_c < 1/(1 + spectral gap)?; the general conjecture needs p_c < p_u even when p_c is close to 1/rho... For groups with p_c(G) < 1/rho(G) the conjecture holds; the remaining case is groups with a Cayley graph where p_c >= 1/rho, and the Pak-Smirnova trick replaces the generating set to make p_c small relative to rho. So the conjecture in its generating-set-free form (some Cayley graph) is settled by Pak-Smirnova, while the conjecture for EVERY Cayley graph reduces to showing p_c(G) < 1/rho(G)^{?}... I checked the inequality p_c <= 1/(1 + h) where h is the Cheeger constant... Benjamini-Schramm prove p_c <= 1/(1+h) and p_u >= 1/(1+h)?? no. The honest reduction: for every Cayley graph, p_c < p_u would follow from p_c < 1/rho (Benjamini-Schramm criterion) and the open question is whether every non-amenable Cayley graph satisfies p_c < 1/rho, which fails? For the free group with the standard generators p_c = 1/(2d-1) and 1/rho = (2d-1)/(2 sqrt(2d-1)) > p_c, consistent. No counterexample and no proof. Obstruction: Need p_c(G) < 1/rho(G) or another uniform criterion for every Cayley graph of every non-amenable group.

OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For a Cayley graph G of a finitely generated infinite group, p_c(G) < p_u(G) if and only if the group is non-amenable. Source: Duminil-Copin: Sixty years of percolation, ICM 2018, Conjecture 2, p. 4. Status notes: Amenable direction is known (Burton-Keane uniqueness gives p_c = p_u). The non-amenable direction is known for many classes (Pak-Smirnova for some generating sets, Hutchcroft for several classes including nonunimodular and hyperbolic settings); not verified in a bounded search whether the full conjecture has been settled by 2026.
Posed in Duminil-Copin: Sixty years of percolation, ICM 2018
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07
rationale: The prescribed simple C_2*C_3 Cayley graph is one nonamenable group/generating-set instance of the universally quantified target.

from_statement_quote: DRAFT AUTHOR MODEL CHECK; independent review pending. In the simple C_2*C_3 triangle graph with one a-edge per unordered pair, the forward branching mean is 2p^2+2p^3-2p^4. Replacing every a-edge by two independent parallel Bernoulli(p) bonds changes its connection probability to 2p-p^2 and the branching mean to 4p^2+2p^3-6p^4+2p^5. Its critical equation is 2p^5-6p^4+2p^3+4p^2-1=0, with root in (0.51,0.53), rather than the simple-graph root in (0.63,0.64). These polynomials are checked by 32 and 128 exact local configurations respectively. Kozakova 2008 reports the latter polynomial with Cayley edge multiplicity; that published number must not be transplanted into the simple graph at the same p.
